parts.problemMd:
A student has set up a password for his laptop computer. The password he has chosen is Px2zY!Cg3?bd

**Discuss **the benefits and drawbacks of using this password.
parts.solutionMd:
The student’s password Px2zY!Cg3?bd is **strong and secure** because it is long and contains a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters, making it **harder to crack** using brute force attacks. Additionally, it **does not contain personal information, which reduces the risk of someone guessing it**. The password’s** length also makes shoulder surfing more difficult**, as it is harder for someone nearby to memorise.

However, the **complexity of the password makes it difficult to remember,** which could lead to the **user writing it down, increasing the risk of unauthorised access**. The **mix of letters, numbers, and symbols may also cause confusion**, such as mistaking ‘2’ for ‘Z’ or ‘1’ for ‘I’, making it **easier to mistype**. Additionally, the user may need to look at the keyboard while typing, slowing down the login process.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> To gain full marks you **must **have correct answers for both benefits and drawbacks
> 
> - Strong password that is hard to crack **[1 mark]**
> - More secure as it does not contain personal information **[1 mark]**
> - Longer password reduces the risk of shoulder surfing **[1 mark]**
> - Difficult to remember due to complexity **[1 mark]**
> - May need to be written down, increasing security risks **[1 mark]**
> - Letters and numbers may be confused, leading to typing errors **[1 mark]**
> 
> **[Total marks: 6/6]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> **Five **top tips for answering this 6-mark "Discuss" question effectively:
> 
> 1. **Include both benefits and drawbacks**
> 
>   1. The mark scheme requires both positive and negative aspects, so make sure to balance your answer.
> 2. **Be specific about security advantages**
> 
>   1. Instead of saying "it is secure," explain why: "It includes a mix of characters, making brute force attacks more difficult."
> 3. **Consider real-world usability issues**
> 
>   1. Mention practical problems, such as difficulty remembering the password or the need to look at the keyboard while typing.
> 4. **Use comparative phrases to strengthen the discussion**
> 
>   1. Example: "Although the password is strong, its complexity may lead to the user writing it down, reducing security."
>   2. This links the benefits and drawbacks, showing a balanced discussion.
> 5. **Avoid vague points and repetition**
> 
>   1. Instead of "it is hard to remember," specify why: "Its combination of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols makes it harder to memorise."
>   2. Cover distinct issues instead of repeating the same idea in different words.

Another issue is that** time zone differences can make scheduling difficult**, especially when **employees are in different parts of the world**. This can lead to meetings being held at inconvenient times for some participants, reducing productivity.

Additionally, video-conferencing may **require specialist hardware and software**, which **can be expensive for companies to purchase and maintain**. Businesses may also need to invest in training staff to use the system effectively, which takes time and resources.

> 
> - Requires a good/fast/reliable internet connection → documents/images may require more bandwidth **[2 marks]**
> - Time zone differences → staff work in other parts of the world/time of meeting may be difficult **[2 marks]**
> - Requires specialist hardware/software → can be expensive to purchase **[2 marks]**
> 
> **[Total marks: 6/6]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> **Five **top tips for answering this 6-mark "describe" question effectively:
> 
> 1. **Use a clear structure with matched pairs**
> 
>   1. Each disadvantage should be followed by a reason/explanation.
>   2. Example: "Time zone differences can make scheduling difficult, as staff work in different parts of the world."
> 2. **Avoid vague or one-word answers**
> 
>   1. Instead of just saying "internet issues", explain "a slow or unstable internet connection can cause delays, affecting communication."
> 3. **Use business-related terminology where possible**
> 
>   1. Terms like "bandwidth," "productivity," "specialist hardware," and "real-time communication" demonstrate a stronger understanding of the topic.
> 4. **Prioritise practical challenges businesses face**
> 
>   1. Think about real-world workplace issues, such as team collaboration, costs, and technical difficulties.

parts.problemMd: **Compare **the similarities and differences between Bluetooth and wi-fi.
parts.solutionMd:
Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are both **wireless communication** technologies that use **radio frequencies to transmit data** securely. They also** allow multiple devices** to connect simultaneously.

However, Wi-Fi has a **faster data transfer rate** than Bluetooth, making it more suitable for tasks that require high bandwidth. Additionally, Wi-Fi has **a greater range**, typically up to 100 metres, whereas Bluetooth is limited to 30 metres. Finally, Wi-Fi can** connect more devices at once**, whereas Bluetooth has a maximum of seven connections.

> **Differences **
> 
> - wi-fi has a faster data transfer rate **[1 mark]**
> - wi-fi has a greater range of transmission **[1 mark]**
> - wi-fi connects more devices **[1 mark]**

Users access cloud storage by **connecting to the internet** and sending files to a remote data server, which is managed by a cloud storage provider. Cloud storage **allows data to be accessed from any device**, making it easy to share files with others. Additionally, cloud providers offer **automatic backups**, ensuring that if one server fails, another can be used as a backup. Some services require users to pay a monthly or annual fee based on the amount of storage used.

parts.problemMd:

**Discuss **the advantages and disadvantages of analysing a system by interviewing staff rather than using questionnaires.
parts.solutionMd:
Analysing a system using interviews instead of questionnaires has several advantages. One benefit is that the interviewer can **clarify any misunderstood questions**, ensuring accurate responses. Additionally, interviews allow for **more detailed answers**, as follow-up questions can be asked based on the interviewee’s responses. Another advantage is that **body language and facial expressions can be observed**, providing extra insight into the interviewee’s opinions.

However, interviews also have disadvantages. **They are not anonymous**, meaning interviewees may feel uncomfortable giving honest answers, especially if they fear repercussions. Additionally, interviews **take longer to complete** than questionnaires, as each person must be spoken to individually. Another drawback is that interviews are** more expensive**, as they require trained interviewers and time off work for staff.

Overall, while interviews provide detailed and flexible responses, questionnaires are quicker, cheaper, and allow for anonymous feedback.

parts.problemMd:
Different methods can be used to analyse a system.

**Discuss** the benefits and drawbacks of analysing a system by observing staff rather than looking at the current systems documentation.
parts.solutionMd:
Analysing a system by observing staff instead of examining documents has several benefits. One advantage is that the **analyst sees the system in action**, allowing them to understand how staff interact with it in real time. Additionally, observation **provides a complete picture** of the system, including any inefficiencies that might not be recorded in documents. Another benefit is that it is less disruptive to workers, as they can continue their tasks while the analyst observes, **making it a cheaper method of analysis**.

However, observation also has drawbacks. The **quality and accuracy of the findings depend on the skill of the observer**, meaning mistakes or biases could affect the results. Another issue is the Hawthorne effect, where staff may change their behaviour when they know they are being watched, leading to inaccurate data.

On the other hand, examining existing documentation has advantages, such as **allowing the analyst to see exact details of inputs, processing, and outputs**, which can be more precise than observation. Additionally, previous system analysis reports may already exist, saving time in the research process. However, looking through documents is **time-consuming**, and hiring an analyst to examine records can be expensive.

Overall, while observation provides real-world insight into system usage, examining documents offers structured and precise information, though it requires more time and cost.

> 
> - The analyst sees the system in action **[1 mark]**
> - Observation provides a complete picture **[1 mark]**
> - Cheaper as it does not take the worker away from work **[1 mark]**
> - The quality and accuracy of information is highly dependent on the skill of the observer **[1 mark]**
> - Examining documents shows exact details of inputs, processing, and outputs **[1 mark]**
> - Very time-consuming to look through all the documents **[1 mark]**

parts.problemMd:

Questionnaires and interviews are examples of methods of researching existing systems.

**Evaluate**, by weighing up the advantages and disadvantages, each of these methods.
parts.solutionMd:
Both questionnaires and interviews are useful methods for researching an existing system, but each has its advantages and disadvantages.

One advantage of questionnaires is that they are **quicker to complete**, allowing multiple people to respond at the same time. Additionally, questionnaires can be **completed in the respondent’s own time**, providing flexibility compared to interviews, which must be scheduled. Another key benefit is that responses can **remain anonymous**, making people more likely to give honest feedback.

However, questionnaires are** inflexible**, as they only allow for fixed responses, whereas interviews can be adjusted based on previous answers. Another drawback is that **respondents may not return questionnaires**, leading to a low response rate. Additionally, if a question is unclear, there is no way for the respondent to ask for clarification, which could result in misleading or inaccurate answers.

On the other hand, interviews allow for deeper discussions, as the interviewer can ask follow-up questions and adapt them based on previous responses. This makes them more flexible and allows for more detailed insights. However, interviews are **more expensive**, as businesses must pay for an interviewer and compensate employees for their time. Additionally, interviews are not anonymous, which may lead some respondents to withhold honest opinions.

Overall, questionnaires are more efficient for collecting large amounts of data, while interviews provide more detailed, flexible responses. The choice of method depends on the time, budget, and depth of information required.

One important measure is to **use anti-spyware and keep antivirus software up to date**, as this helps prevent malware from stealing personal information. Additionally, gamers should always keep their **firewall enabled**, as it blocks unauthorised access to their system while playing online.

Another key safety measure is to **download games and updates only from reputable sources**. This ensures that players do not install pirated or modified versions that could contain malware. Furthermore, **choosing a username that does not reveal personal information** helps protect users from identity theft or unwanted contact from strangers.

To further enhance security, gamers should** delete their account details if they stop playing a game**, preventing hackers from accessing their old profiles. Finally, when disposing of a gaming device, **all personal information should be erased**, ensuring that no sensitive data remains stored on the system.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Use anti-spyware/up-to-date antivirus software **[1 mark]**
> - Play with the firewall operational **[1 mark]**
> - Download/buy files and new software from reputable sources **[1 mark]**
> - Choose a username that does not reveal any personal information **[1 mark]**
> - Delete account details when no longer playing **[1 mark]**
> - Ensure personal information is deleted when disposing of a gaming device **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> **Five **top tips for answering this 6-mark "describe" question effectively:
> 
> 1. **List six distinct safety measures**
> 
>   1. Avoid repeating similar points (e.g., don’t list both "use antivirus" and "use anti-spyware" as separate points).
> 2. **Explain why each measure improves security**
> 
>   1. Instead of just saying "use a firewall," write "keep the firewall enabled to block unauthorised access while gaming online."
> 3. **Consider both software and personal habits**
> 
>   1. Mention software-based protection (antivirus, firewalls, updates) and user behaviour (choosing safe usernames, deleting account details).
> 4. **Avoid vague statements**
> 
>   1. Instead of saying "stay safe online," specify how, e.g., "choose a username that does not reveal real names or personal details to protect identity."
> 5. **Think beyond gameplay**
> 
>   1. Include precautions before, during, and after gaming, such as deleting personal information when disposing of a device.

parts.problemMd:
The data stored on the computer system needs to be protected from unauthorised access

**Discuss** the effectiveness of different methods of increasing security of this data.
parts.solutionMd:
There are several methods to increase the security of data on a computer system, each with varying levels of effectiveness.

One effective method is using **strong passwords**, as they are harder to crack than simple passwords. Additionally, **biometric authentication is even more secure** since it relies on unique human characteristics, making it nearly impossible to duplicate. **Two-factor authentication (2FA) **further improves security by requiring an extra layer of verification, such as a code sent to a mobile device. **Firewalls** also play a key role by **blocking unauthorised access** and preventing fraudulent websites from attacking the computer. Lastly, anti-spyware software helps prevent keyloggers from capturing passwords, reducing the risk of credential theft.

However, security methods also have limitations. Overly** complex passwords can be easily forgotten**, leading users to write them down or reset them frequently. Additionally, r**egularly changing passwords can make them easier to guess** if users follow predictable patterns. **Firewalls**, while essential for security, **can sometimes block legitimate software and may need to be temporarily disabled**, making the system vulnerable during updates. Lastly, **hackers can still breach even strong passwords**, particularly if a user reuses them across multiple accounts.

Overall, while strong passwords, biometric authentication, firewalls, and 2FA improve security, they also introduce challenges related to usability and system performance. A balanced approach that includes multiple security layers is the most effective way to protect sensitive data.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> You must include at least four advantages and four disadvantages, ensuring a balanced discussion
> 
> - Strong passwords are difficult to crack **[1 mark]**
> - Biometric passwords are harder to crack **[1 mark]**
> - Two-factor authentication adds extra security **[1 mark]**
> - Firewalls prevent unauthorised access **[1 mark]**
> - Too complex passwords can be easily forgotten **[1 mark]**
> - Regularly changing passwords makes them easier to guess **[1 mark]**
> - Firewalls may block legitimate software and require disabling for updates **[1 mark]**
> - Hackers can still breach strong passwords **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> **Five **top tips for answering this 8-mark "discuss" question effectively:
> 
> 1. **Include both advantages and disadvantages**
>

> 2. **Explain why certain methods improve security**
> 
>   1. Example: Instead of just saying "2FA increases security," write "2FA adds an extra layer of protection by requiring a second form of authentication, making it harder for hackers to gain access."
> 3. **Acknowledge the limitations of security measures**
> 
>   1. Mention real-world issues like "firewalls blocking legitimate software" and "passwords being difficult to remember if changed too often."
> 4. **Compare effectiveness vs. practicality**
> 
>   1. Example: "While biometric authentication is highly secure, it requires expensive hardware and may not always work reliably."
> 5. **Avoid vague points**

parts.problemMd:

Controlling the freedom of speech is part of policing the internet.

**Discuss **whether the internet should be policed or not.
parts.solutionMd:
Policing the internet has several benefits. One key advantage is that it **prevents illegal material from being readily available**, helping to reduce harmful content such as illegal activities and explicit material. Additionally, it **protects young children from accessing unsuitable material**, ensuring they are not exposed to inappropriate content. Another benefit is that it helps enforce copyright laws, preventing people from illegally sharing or downloading protected content.

However, policing the internet also has drawbacks. **Governments may block certain viewpoints, leading to biased control over information**. Additionally, **policing the internet would be difficult to enforce**, as new content is constantly being uploaded worldwide. Another issue is that it could reduce internet usage, as users may feel like they are constantly monitored, creating a "Big Brother" effect.

Overall, while policing the internet can protect users and reduce illegal activity, it also raises concerns about government control, enforcement challenges, and freedom of speech.

> 
> - Prevents illegal material from being readily available **[1 mark]**
> - Prevents young children from accessing unsuitable material **[1 mark]**
> - Governments block viewpoints based on their own bias **[1 mark]**
> - Policing the internet is difficult to enforce **[1 mark]**

>

> 
>   1. Instead of saying "policing is hard," write "new content is constantly uploaded, making enforcement difficult."

parts.problemMd: **Discuss **the disadvantages of policing the internet.
parts.solutionMd:
Policing the internet has several disadvantages. One major concern is that it **removes freedom of speech**, as governments or organisations may decide what content is allowed, potentially leading to biased restrictions. Additionally, the** internet is international, making it difficult to police effectively**, as laws vary between countries and enforcement would be inconsistent.

Another issue is that **criminal activity may shift to the dark net**, **where it is even harder to track**. Similarly, **electronic crimes could move away from the internet, making them more difficult for law enforcement to intercept**. Furthermore, internet users can remain anonymous, meaning tracking illegal activity is challenging and often ineffective.

Policing the internet also raises privacy concerns, as constant monitoring could make users feel like they are always being watched. Additionally, **the cost of security would increase**, requiring significant investment in surveillance and enforcement.

Overall, while policing the internet aims to improve security, it presents significant challenges related to freedom, enforcement, cost, and privacy.

> - International, therefore difficult to police **[1 mark]**

> - Increase in the cost of security **[1 mark]**

parts.problemMd:
Two types of database are relational and flat file.

**Compare **and **contrast **relational databases and flat file databases.

Your answer **must **include similarities and differences.
parts.solutionMd:
Both relational databases and flat file databases share some similarities. They **both use a primary key** to uniquely identify records, ensuring data integrity. Additionally, both types of databases **store data in records and fields** within a table format. Another similarity is that both can **create searches and reports**, allowing users to retrieve and present data efficiently.

However, there are several differences between them. A flat file database **consists of a single table**, whereas a relational database has **multiple linked tables** that can establish relationships between different datasets. Flat file databases are simpler in structure and typically stored as plain text files, whereas relational databases **use foreign keys** to link records across tables, making them more powerful and **reducing data duplication**. Additionally, relational databases **allow searches and reports to be created across multiple tables**, providing more efficient data management and retrieval.

Overall, while both database types store and manage data, relational databases offer greater flexibility, scalability, and efficiency due to their structured relationships and ability to prevent redundancy.

> **[mark-scheme]**

> 
> - Both use a primary key **[1 mark]**
> - Both can create searches/reports **[1 mark]**
> - Both store data in records and fields in a table **[1 mark]**
> - Flat file uses one table **[1 mark]**
> - Relational database has linked tables/relationships **[1 mark]**
> - Relational database allows searches/reports to be created over multiple tables **[1 mark]**
> - Relational database reduces duplicate data **[1 mark]**
> - Relational database uses foreign keys **[1 mark]**
>

parts.problemMd: **Discuss **the use of layers in the development of a webpage.
parts.solutionMd:
Webpages are typically developed using **three distinct layers**: **content**, **presentation**, and **behaviour**. Each layer has a specific role and contributes to a more structured and manageable development process.

The **content layer** is responsible for the structure and information on the webpage. It includes **text, images, headings, and links**, and is usually written using **HTML**. This layer forms the foundation of the site’s information.

The **presentation layer** controls how the content looks. This includes the **layout, fonts, colours, and overall styling** of the page. It is handled using **CSS (Cascading Style Sheets)**, which ensures that the appearance of the site is consistent and easily adjustable.

The **behaviour layer** adds interactivity and dynamic features to the webpage. This can include **form validation, animations, and interactive menus**, and is typically implemented using **JavaScript**.

Using a layered approach has several benefits. Each layer can be **developed and updated independently**, which makes maintaining and improving the site more efficient. It also allows **specialist developers to work on separate areas**—such as designers focusing on CSS and developers working on JavaScript—leading to **faster and more organised development** overall.

> - Describes the **content layer** (structure, HTML) **[1 mark]**
> - Describes the **presentation layer** (appearance, CSS) **[1 mark]**
> - Describes the **behaviour layer** (interactivity, JavaScript) **[1 mark]**
> - Explains that layers can be developed independently **[1 mark]**
> - Explains that specialists can work on different layers for efficient development **[1 mark]**
>

parts.problemMd:
A sales representative is planning a presentation about a new product.

He is considering whether to use a multimedia presentation or to give a talk and hand out leaflets.

**Discuss **the advantages and disadvantages of using a multimedia presentation rather than printed leaflets.
parts.solutionMd:
Using a **multimedia presentation** instead of printed leaflets has several advantages for a sales representative. One key benefit is that **multimedia allows for the use of sound, video, animations, and transitions**, making the presentation more engaging and helping to capture the audience’s attention. It can also be **more interactive**, with the use of hyperlinks or clickable elements, allowing it to be shared online or used on an interactive whiteboard. Another advantage is that **there are no printing costs**, and the presentation is **easier to update**, especially if product information changes. Multimedia presentations can also be **more accessible**, for example, by using text-to-speech features for visually impaired users.

However, there are also disadvantages. **Special equipment is needed**, such as a computer, projector, or speakers, which may not always be available. **Technical issues** like power cuts, equipment failure, or corrupted files could disrupt the presentation. Additionally, **some users may focus more on the visuals and animations rather than the product content**. Unlike leaflets, **audience members need to be present** to see the presentation, whereas a leaflet **can be read at any time** and taken away for future reference. Furthermore, **presentations cannot be produced in braille**, making printed leaflets more suitable for certain accessibility needs.
